_what: Every shape one half of a check's Pass / Fail line can take, as the fixture that produces it and the line it must draw. THE DEFINITION, not a description of one: tools/GameHarness turns each row into an in-game suite, and tests/branch_shapes.rs runs the same row through the engine over the shipped index. Adding a row adds a test to both; neither side declares anything of its own.
_colours: orange = unseen in any game, red = unseen this game, darkRed = already read in this save. A marker is one of those three, or gaveUp for a search that did not finish, or absent where nothing beyond the destination outranks it.
_extra: A row is the whole scenario, and both executors read all of it. If one ever needs something the other cannot use - an in-game screenshot reference, say - it goes under a key naming the executor, 'offline' or 'inGame', so a reader can see at a glance which half of the world it belongs to. NOTHING NEEDS THAT YET and no support for it is built; what the offline executor needs beyond these fields, it reads from the same save the in-game one loads.
_eight: orange alone (nothing outranks the top rung, so it never carries a marker); red alone, red+orange, red+gaveUp; darkRed alone, darkRed+red, darkRed+orange, darkRed+gaveUp. Rows both differ across the two halves and match, which is what says the halves are read separately.
